ACCESS is the other catch: the prospectus reserves 'Selected Retail Investors' classes to retail investors who are senior management of the Investment Manager, plus platforms, selected at the Board's discretion. The 0.60% classes B and RAE pay a 10% performance fee over EUR STR worth ~2 pts of average class NAV in a strong trend year. Platform-visible siblings IAET (LU1662498721) and the flat-fee IAE1FT (LU2622190622) are catalogued separately and carry their own backcasts; IAE1FT bears the same 1.00% management INSIDE its NAV, with no waiver to lose. Two more things the NAV does not show: the fund takes its exposure through an UNFUNDED total return swap with Morgan Stanley plus a funding swap rather than by holding futures, so counterparty concentration is real; and this is an 'Absolute Return' book (trend plus macro plus short-term), not a pure CTA, which is the source of its low 0.50 correlation with the DBi replication book and the reason not to ask it for a pure trend follower's work in an oil shock.
